newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-S.African insurers set for strong results.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-S.African insurers set for strong results.

text.p: South African insurers Liberty Life Association of Africa Ltd and Fedsure Holdings Ltd are set to post a bumper crop of year results next week, analysts said on Friday.
Neither firm has any great exposure to the short-term insurance market and so will side-step the pay-outs associated with South Africa's notorious crime wave.
However, analysts said the reasons for the firms' strong performances differ with Fedsure relying on its new diversifed interests and Liberty benefitting from historical strengths.

On Monday Fedsure is set to post year earnings per share on a range of 119.6 cents to 124.0 cents, up from 97.6 cents last time. A dividend on a range of 86.5 cents to 88.3 cents is forecast, up from 69.5 cents.
The consensus figures are earnings of 122.2 cents a share and a payout to shareholders of 87.0 cents a share.
Due to the insurance industry's high level of reserves analysts said firms almost had a blank cheque to boost or decrease their stated levels of earnings.

Analysts said it is widely rumoured in the market that Fedsure will bring out a sparkling set of results. "I wouldn't be surprised at all to see a high figure. It is widely known that they will do well," said one analyst.
Fedsure's shares were trading as low as 27.00 rand in December, but now stand at almost 38.00 rand. "Something leaked into the market," one analyst said.
"They have not got the same quality of life business as the others, but they are making it up by diversifying," said Clive Cook, analyst at BOE NatWest.
Liberty, on the other hand, will benefit from its traditional strengths.
Liberty will post its year results on Thursday and analysts are forecasting earnings per share on a range of 598 cents to 637 cents, up from 498.4 last time.
A dividend increase to 320 cents from 256 cents has already been announced.
The firm will continue to reap rewards from a high number of individual policy holders with inflation-linked premiums and its underlying asset performance is strong, analysts said.
In particular the firm has a 72 percent holding in Britain's fourth largest quoted property firm Capital Shopping Centres Plc through Liberty International Holdings.

Capital, which has five of Britain's top 10 shopping centres and 155 million customers a year, has had a strong year in sterling terms and this will translate into an even more hefty profit in rand, analysts said.
Liberty also has huge reserves that could top up the earnings, if necessary.
"Most of this is historical. They have got enough fat to maintain their earnings growth," one analyst said.
